previous_disclosures.section: Operating Segment Trends and Results > Cost of Sales
previous_disclosures.summary: Cost of sales increased by $4.1 billion to $25.6 billion in 2024, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation for manufacturing assets (mostly Intel 7 process node), $1.3 billion in higher intersegment COGS due to volume and advanced tech ramp, and factory start-up costs.

Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.

current_disclosures.section: Consolidated Results of Operations > Liquidity and Capital Resources > Critical Accounting Estimates > Property, Plant and Equipment
current_disclosures.summary: Intel evaluates the recoverable period for property, plant, and equipment annually, using management judgments on useful lives. In 2025 and 2024, shortening useful lives for certain placed-in-service equipment resulted in accelerated depreciation charges of $456 million and $992 million, respectively, as manufacturing asset portfolios exceeded capacity requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation Allowance for Deferred Tax Assets
comparisons.peer_summary: As of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, the company had valuation allowances of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, for capital loss carryforwards and certain state and other deferred tax assets not likely to be realized.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose specific monetary amounts for valuation allowances recorded against deferred tax assets, highlighting the materiality of this line item in their financial results. Intel reported a massive $9.9 billion non-cash charge related to valuation allowances on net deferred tax assets in 2024, whereas NVIDIA disclosed smaller valuation allowances of $1.6 billion for capital loss carryforwards and certain state deferred tax assets. While both companies recognize the need for such allowances, the scale and primary drivers differ significantly, with Intel's charge reflecting broader asset impairment and profitability challenges compared to NVIDIA's more targeted carryforward protections.

sentences.text: ■$9.9 billion of non-cash charges recorded to provision for income taxes that substantially related to valuation allowances recorded to our net deferred tax assets (see "Note 8: Income Taxes" within Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements).

As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, we had a valuation allowance of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards, and certain state and other deferred tax assets that management determined are not likely to be realized due, in part, to jurisdictional projections of future taxable income, including capital gains.
